Watching the trailer, I saw lots of really awesome stuff that could be put into a new game to take the mayor job to the next level next time. I'm not sure what a lot of things in the trailer meant, but it looked like you could build various types of buildings and set them up however you want. What if in the next game there was a preset list of building types you could place around your town (restaurant, arcade, movie theater, gym, etc), set up the interior, and villagers would have the AI built in to use those buildings based on what building type you set them to? It sounds like a lot to expect, but based on HHA I'm thinking it might actually happen.

Of course, in a main series entry you wouldn't have access to all of the furniture like you do in HHD. But that would make it better. Collecting furniture is one of the funnest parts of the games, and this would give you more incentive to collect it. You would need to collect furniture not just for your house, but for all the various buildings you have set up around town!

Another thing I saw in the trailer was OUTDOOR FURNITURE. I'm really psyched about that, and that's the thing I see as being most likely to make it into the next real game. Finally we can have a real backyard.
How do you think the features shown in Happy Home Designer might be integrated into the next main series entry?

Personally, I'm really hoping that our ability to build different structures in the spin-off translates to the mayor being able to choose where new villager's houses are placed when they move in. So no more ruined sidewalks, no more destroyed flowers/trees, and no more villagers moving too close to your home. Maybe, as the mayor, we could coordinate with Nook in the house-building process when a new animal moves in. As an added bonus, Tom Nook would get some more screen time, which I felt he was missing in his new role in New Leaf.

Also, I hope this means placing structures outside will be a whole lot easier. We'll have the Wii U tablet, so why not let us use the touch screen to place a bench or whatever? That would be better then trying to guess the position based on where you're standing. Also, maybe we could work with Lief on occasion to do some serious landscaping instead of moving a couple flowers at a time. Although, the amount of work I put into my village makes it really feel like it's mine, so industrializing it so much might make the game feel less personal. At the very least, I hope we have some say in where people move in. Or at least set off-limit zones. Basically, I just hope HHD gives the devs some ideas to give the mayor some more work to do.

Can jumping genes cause cancer chaos?

Okay, this idea that the genome is comprised of 2% of functional DNA while the remaining 98% is junk has got to go. The truth is we are finding more and more about the role of "junk DNA" every day. Current science shows that a significant portion of it is responsible for helping to regulate gene expression. The mere fact that gene expression deregulation is critical for generating cells more likely to become malignant should demonstrate the importance of the remaining 98%.

To address the jumping genes: transposons have been known for ages. We learned much about them through experimentation with the household fruit fly. And since it's been established for a while that lysogenic viruses, that integrate their genome into a host cell can disrupt a tumor suppressor gene or serve to promote expression of an oncognene, it's well known that things that jump can be a factor in causing cancer. Endogenous genes most likely have that potential, too. Just as some genetic predispositions exist that allow premature disease manifestation, surely genes that migrate more than usual, or have a defective entry point into a genome may exert the same deleterious effect.
